note: Round 12 (Larus GL-2). Not gate files. Every number was measured by the scripts named (scratchpad r12/ is the physics agent's scratch directory; evidence copied under out/sweep/round12/). eta_s 0.6 default unless stated.

rows.tag: 1 M5 approach-and-flare law (controller law, SPEC ruling after round 11)
rows.method: src/physics/control.js landingLaw in the controller ("land" mode) at its 240 Hz rate, on pitot airspeed and baro/IMU height and climb rate, through the 20 ms delay line: approach PI on airspeed with the feed-forward from the approach speed's own glide row; exponential flare latched below flareH = tau x approach sink (tau 1.5 s, touchdown sink command 0.3 m/s, kS 0.3); stall guard at 1.1 Vs. Approach speed VREF = 1.23 x the reference stall speed (14 CFR 25.125(b)(2)(i)), the stall speed being the slowest converged steady parked-wing glide trim over nominal and the 8 corners (src/design/round12.mjs landingLawFor, to 0.05 m/s). runM5 adds "no stall departure" (M4's definition) to its pass rule.
rows.on_v20: v20 with the law (Vapp 8.92 = 1.23 x 7.25): touchdown 7.99-8.55 m/s, sink <= 0.71 m/s at all 9 corners x 2 seeds, no stall departure (scratchpad r12/m5runs-v2.log); the old law touched down at 9.76 m/s. Approach at 9.43 (1.3 Vs) failed 18/18 at 9.15-9.48 m/s; the flare gains were chosen on this sweep (r12/m5b.log).
rows.tests: test/physics/round12.test.js (approach, flare, guard, bounds, pass rule against hand calculations)

rows.tag: 2 gear life factors (SPEC ruling after round 11)
rows.method: src/physics/gears.js KL_TABLE / KHL_TABLE (JGMA 401-01 / 402-01 as KHK Tables 10.2 / 10.10 print them; KHK Japanese PDF and the SDP/SI-numbered copy agree; scratchpad research/round12-parts.json Q1), a count taking the row at or above it (no source states a rule between rows); K_L on bending, K_HL squared on surface; Duracon from KHK Fig. 11.3 read off the curve less 0.05 kgf/mm2 (no printed numbers). src/design/gearing.js lifeCycles: 200 flights x flight_s x the gear's own rpm at the rating crank frequency.
rows.result: no credit where it matters: the binding members are the fast Duracon stages (> 1e6 cycles: 8.9e6-1.5e7) and the last-stage MSGA1-18 pinion (1.1e6 cycles at 3 Hz and 743 s, just past the 1e6 row); only the slow crank wheels (4.5e5 cycles) gain K_L 1.1 / K_HL 1.15, and they are not binding. v20's train stays 16.24 N m at the crank. Every lighter or stronger train found by r12/trainsearch12.mjs with life factors is set by the same members.

rows.tag: 2b latent M7 rating-condition failure on v20
rows.finding: v20's M4 population reaches a peak crank rate of 3.20 Hz (r12/m4a.log) against the 3.0 Hz its train was rated at; missions.mjs M7 checks speed_within, so v20 would have failed M7 on the rating condition. v21 rates its train at 4.0 Hz; its flown peak is 3.83 Hz.

src/physics/structure.js mixedMeshCheck fails a steel-on-Duracon mesh unless both members carry a published allowable surface stress, and no catalogue gear does. v19/v20's trains (MSGA1-20 / DS1-64, and DSF1-24's SUS303 hub read as steel against DS1-36) and the first v21 (SSG1-15 / DS1-64) all mesh steel with Duracon; missions.mjs was last run on v17 (no mixed mesh), so it was never reported. The first v21 failed M7 on it alone (scratchpad r12/v21a-M7-nominal.json: everything else in M7 passed, FoS >= 1.72). trainsearch12.mjs --no-mixed: the lightest train with no mixed mesh is 432.5 g (G 41.7), 86 g more than the 346 g mixed train.

rows.tag: 3 servo regulator, 3S packs and the motor
rows.method: build.js regulatorServoSupply (p.servoSupply "regulator", parts.servoRegulator): torque and speed at the published output less its 4% accuracy, or the lowest pack voltage less the dropout read off the curve; stall current at output + 4% (existing V/V_top rule above the top current row); battery draw at that voltage through the lower end of the published typical efficiency. flight.js draws the regulator's power from the pack; missions.mjs M8 checks the servo peak against its published continuous output. Catalogue: 4 Pololu regulators (S/r12/cat12.py, research/round12-parts.json Q3).
rows.what_if: v20 with its pack at 3 cells (scratchpad r12/whatif3s-*): stroke cap x1.1 / x1.2 gave M4 98 / 100 nominal; M1 3.03 / 4.46 m (worse: more frequency at the 8 m/s release stalls the outer wing).
rows.screens: r12/b/: sc47 (Scorpion SII-3008-1090, G 47.4) M4 100/98/100 but crank 16.8/17.9 N m; sc40 (G 40) M4 100/99/100, crank 15.3/16.2, coupler 1714 N (FoS 1.25); lower stroke caps RAISE the crank peak (16.13 at x0.94); the drive clamp at 26 A cuts it to 14.0/15.3 with M4 100/99 (r12/b/sc40-clamp.log).

rows.method: control.js launchLaw: pitch "speed" (PI on a climb-out airspeed) or the existing climb law, and a launch stroke frequency freq_Hz.
rows.result_v20: speed-hold laws 2.76-4.25 m worst (worse than the climb law, 2.38); climb command 1.5 / 6 m/s, stall-pitch gain 0.03 / 0.2, twist cap 45 / 52 deg: 2.38-2.48; launch frequency 1.9-2.45 Hz: best 2.338 at 2.45 (r12/m1a-c.log, m1b.log).
rows.result_v21: v21 (envelope 3.33 Hz): own law 2.92 m; launch at 2.4 / 2.6 / 2.8 / 3.0 Hz on the 1588 g build: 2.18 / 2.15 / 2.32 / 2.48 m (r12/b/sc40m4-m1.log); v21 flies 2.6 Hz. On the final 1708 g v21 the launch frequency no longer matters: 2.3 / 2.45 / 2.6 / 2.75 / 2.9 Hz give a worst 2.942 / 2.935 / 2.921 / 2.915 / 2.926 m (r12/v21-m1-launch.log).
rows.physics: Static flapping trims (r12/flaptrim*.log): level flight needs >= 9.25 m/s nominal even at 38 deg twist (9.0 m/s needs 4.8 Hz); the worst corner cannot trim at 9.5. From an 8 m/s release the kinetic energy to reach that floor alone is (9.25^2 - 8^2)/2g = 1.1 m nominal and about 1.5-1.7 m at aero 0.9 / mass 1.05.

rows.finding: Failures are sustained Dryden downdrafts beyond the climb power (seed 15: -2.5 m/s for 7 s, r12/m4trace.mjs). Vrough 16 / 17 and TECS spdWeight 0.2 did not help (93-96/100, r12/m4a.log). The 3S drive closes it (see 3 and the gate table).

Nothing the rules do not require was found to remove: the round-12 member probes show the 3S stroke speeds load the shoulder rails, lock screws, brackets, side panels, coupler and crank 1.3-1.6x harder, so v21 sizes them up (+27 g with margin) and the stroke envelope now keeps 0.6 of every member rating (trim.js membersRatio, opt-in). Members sit at FoS 1.66 and up on the nominal population (M7). Against v20: tail servos HV6160 -> Hitec MD89MW (-18 g), motor C-2820 -> Scorpion SII-3008-1090 (-45 g), 3S pack +39 g, regulator +7 g, gears +66 g (no-mixed train, 437 g), drive linkage and plates +50 g, margin +15 g: 1708.3 g.

KHK publishes Duracon's maximum allowable surface stress only as a curve for a Duracon/Duracon pair (Technical Reference Fig. 11.7, m 2, 12 m/s, room temperature, unlubricated basis), read at about 32 MPa at 1e6 and 24 MPa at 1e7 cycles; no maker rates the steel/Duracon pair. Hertz (structure.js hertzSpur, steel 205.9 GPa / 0.3, Duracon 2.7 GPa / 0.35, b 6 mm) at the flown pinion torques gives 78.9 MPa on the first v21's SSG1-15/DS1-64 and 72.0 MPa on v20's MSGA1-20/DS1-64: even if the curve were admitted, both meshes would fail by 2-3x. The no-mixed train is therefore required, not only a reading of the rule.
